title: Forward Deployment Engineering for Leaders
headline: Lead AI from a promising demo to a governed decision.
intro: A C-suite learning experience for selecting useful AI opportunities, funding bounded pilots, assigning ownership and making evidence-based decisions about adoption.
audience: C-suite leaders, business heads and transformation sponsors
bridge: No coding prerequisite. Bring familiarity with a business workflow, its stakeholders and the decisions you need to make. Technical concepts are explored through demonstrations, proposal reviews and leadership exercises.
scope: Designed around AI strategy, investment decisions, governance and adoption. Exercises focus on leadership decisions and do not require coding. The 90-day blueprint is a planning exercise, not a course duration or a guaranteed delivery schedule.
paths: Frame value, baseline measures, decision rights and the investment case for a bounded pilot.
Connect architecture, data readiness, risk ownership and operating-model decisions.

modules.title: AI reality for leaders
modules.summary: Evaluate proposals by capability, evidence and consequences of error.
topics: LLM capabilities, unsupported answers and limitations
RAG, fine-tuning and smaller-model tradeoffs
Agents, reversible actions and human approval
Voice, vision and document-workflow opportunities
tools: Facilitated model demonstrations — inspect success and failure
Capability scorecard — compare a proposal with evidence
Workflow map — locate decisions and escalation
modules.practice: Review a proposal claiming AI can resolve all service tickets. Narrow the ticket classes, permitted actions and evidence requirements, then request a denied-action and unsupported-answer demonstration.
criteria: The proposal has testable scope
Consequential actions have review owners
A fluent demonstration is not treated as proof of reliability

modules.title: Workflow discovery & opportunity framing
modules.summary: Start with a business process and a measurable problem.
topics: Current-state workflow and handoff mapping
Customer, employee and operator perspectives
Task suitability: deterministic software, assistance or bounded automation
Baseline measures and counterfactual questions
Choosing a pilot with a manageable impact boundary
tools: Workflow canvas — map tasks, decisions and exceptions
Interview guide — collect observations rather than solution preferences
Opportunity scorecard — compare value, readiness and uncertainty
modules.practice: Review an illustrative invoice-query workflow. Identify the real delay, interview questions, non-AI alternatives and the smallest useful pilot boundary.
criteria: Connect the proposed capability to an observed problem
Consider simpler process or software changes
Make unresolved assumptions visible before funding

modules.title: Data readiness & architecture choices
modules.summary: Ask the questions that connect a proposal to the organisation’s systems.
topics: Source ownership, access rights and information quality
Retrieval, model adaptation and system integration at a decision level
Identity, permissions and auditability
Vendor dependencies, portability and exit planning
Human review points and failure containment
tools: Architecture canvas — explain systems and trust boundaries
Data-readiness checklist — identify ownership and quality gaps
Build–buy–partner matrix — compare operating responsibilities
modules.practice: Compare a document assistant delivered as a managed service with an internal application. Identify who owns access, corrections, evaluations and the ongoing service.
criteria: Distinguish product claims from evidence available for review
Identify an owner for each data source and access decision
Include ongoing operations when comparing options

modules.title: Prioritise & fund
modules.summary: Choose an opportunity the organisation can responsibly validate.
topics: Workflow discovery and measurable baselines
Data quality, provenance and permission readiness
Build, buy and partner comparisons
Cost assumptions, review effort and sensitivity analysis
tools: Use-case scorecard — compare value, feasibility and risk
Spreadsheet scenario model — test cost/value assumptions
Vendor-question guide — examine integration and exit needs
modules.practice: Compare an internal knowledge assistant, invoice triage and a sales-support workflow. Select one bounded pilot and explain why the alternatives should wait.
criteria: Value is tied to a stated baseline
Review, integration and operating costs are included
Estimates are scenarios rather than promised returns

modules.title: Evaluation, assurance & decision gates
modules.summary: Define the evidence a pilot must produce before it expands.
topics: Task quality, unsupported answers and consequential errors
Representative test sets and adversarial scenarios
Human review effort, latency and total service cost
Pilot gates, acceptance criteria and stop conditions
Independent challenge and escalation responsibilities
tools: Evaluation scorecard — relate evidence to intended use
Scenario library — test ordinary cases and important failures
Decision log — record proceed, revise and pause reasoning
modules.practice: Inspect a sample AI pilot scorecard with strong average results but poor handling of high-impact exceptions. Decide what evidence is missing and whether the scope should change.
criteria: Do not substitute a demo or single metric for acceptance evidence
Define thresholds before reviewing pilot results
Account for human work needed to operate safely

modules.title: Govern & operate
modules.summary: Assign responsibility for safe operation and meaningful adoption.
topics: Risk, human control and stop conditions
Access limits, logs and necessary evidence
Business, technical and incident ownership
Role-specific training, feedback and change management
tools: Risk register — identify owners and controls
RACI — clarify decision and operating responsibilities
Tabletop incident exercise — rehearse escalation
Adoption checklist — define readiness evidence
modules.practice: Map an approval-based invoice workflow. Rehearse an incorrect recommendation, an unauthorised action and an unavailable service, then decide who pauses the pilot.
criteria: Reviewers have evidence, time and authority
Logs do not unnecessarily expose sensitive content
An accountable owner can stop or revise the workflow

modules.title: Adoption, operating model & stakeholder communication
modules.summary: Prepare people and responsibilities alongside the technology.
topics: Process redesign and new ownership responsibilities
Role-based enablement and user feedback
Adoption measures versus business outcomes
Procurement and implementation handovers
Executive updates that separate facts, assumptions and decisions
tools: Responsibility matrix — clarify who decides and operates
Adoption plan — sequence enablement and feedback
Executive update template — present evidence and requested decisions
modules.practice: Prepare a rollout conversation for business users, engineering, security and support. Explain changed responsibilities, the fallback process and how feedback will change the pilot.
criteria: Name accountable owners rather than generic teams alone
Measure actual use and task outcomes separately
Keep open risks and remaining decisions visible

modules.title: The 90-day execution blueprint
modules.summary: Present an evidence-led pilot plan with a genuine stop or scale decision.
topics: Priority use cases and dependency sequencing
Pilot audience, quality measures and baseline
Data, evaluation, user-readiness and incident gates
Leadership review, scope revision and controlled expansion
tools: Pilot charter — scope the experiment
Decision-gate checklist — define evidence and ownership
Executive narrative — present the recommendation
Roadmap template — sequence discovery, pilot and review
modules.practice: Present an illustrative 90-day plan: first establish the baseline and permissions, then run a bounded pilot, then review measured evidence. Explain what would change your recommendation.
criteria: Efficiency measures are paired with quality and risk measures
Dates are planning assumptions, not delivery promises
Stop, revise and scale decisions each have explicit evidence

projects.title: AI opportunity investment brief
projects.problem: Leadership has several attractive proposals but limited delivery capacity.
projects.practice: Compare three illustrative opportunities and present the assumptions behind one priority. Compare the proposed pilot with a process improvement or conventional software alternative. Record value assumptions, readiness gaps, cost categories and the evidence required to justify the next commitment. Present a staged decision rather than a confident forecast unsupported by the available data.
failures: Vendor capability mistaken for organisational readiness

projects.title: A governed operations pilot
projects.problem: Invoice triage could reduce repetitive work, but a wrong action has consequences.
projects.practice: Design the review boundary, ownership and stop conditions using a simulated workflow. Map where a human must approve an action and what happens when information is missing or contradictory. Review sample evaluation results, assign an operating owner and define the conditions for a limited pilot. Include a clear stop condition and a route for users to challenge an output.

projects.title: The executive deployment blueprint
projects.problem: A successful demonstration needs a controlled path into organisational practice.
projects.practice: Prepare and defend a 90-day planning scenario with measurable gates, adoption responsibilities and a handover decision. Sequence discovery, readiness, bounded implementation, evaluation and adoption decisions in an illustrative planning window. Identify dependencies and decision owners, then rehearse a review where one milestone is not met. Revise the plan without treating elapsed time as evidence of readiness.
failures: Metrics reward speed but hide errors

preparation: Ask for baselines, failure examples, access boundaries and a clear operating owner. Ask a team to trace a successful case and an important failure through the proposed system. Identify unsupported assumptions about data access, human review and operational ownership.

Explain value assumptions, total operating effort and what evidence would justify further funding. Present the baseline, cost drivers, learning budget and next decision gate. Explain what would make you reduce the scope or stop, as well as what evidence would justify further work.

Practise pausing or revising a pilot when quality, risk or adoption evidence is inadequate. Work through an exception scenario involving an unsupported answer, permission gap or rising review workload. Assign a decision owner and record whether the pilot should proceed, revise or pause.

Present the charter, accountable owners and stop/scale criteria to business and technical stakeholders. Give business, technology and operations audiences a common account of value, evidence, open risks and ownership. End with a specific decision request and the conditions attached to it.
curriculumTitle: AI leadership curriculum: make the decisions behind deployment.
curriculumIntro: Explore eight executive modules on AI capabilities, opportunity framing, data readiness, funding, evaluation, governance, adoption and a 90-day planning exercise.
